description: Ehsanur Rahman, software engineer with 11 years of shipping apps (50+ apps, 1M+ users) and founder of Hourwise Labs, building AI products. I'll lead the build and the web app.
summary: NASA is preparing to put astronauts in 34% oxygen on the Moon, yet most of its spacecraft fire data was measured in orbit near normal air. FlameSense turns that gap into clear answers. It is a free web app built on 123 cited NASA microgravity and partial-gravity combustion test runs (BASS, BASS-II, Saffire and partial-gravity flight tests), plus all 24 combustion investigations in NASA's PSI Data Repository. Pick a mission (ISS, Artemis lunar habitat, Mars transit or Mars surface) and FlameSense shows each material's worst-case chance of burning, how fast a flame would spread, and how strongly NASA's data supports that answer. Where the data runs out, it says so instead of guessing, and it ranks the five untested conditions NASA should test next. Machine-learning models trained on NASA runs work right in the browser, a flame-spread physics model checks them, and an Ask page answers questions only from NASA documents, with every sentence cited. FlameSense helps mission planners, researchers and students see fire risk in space honestly, and carries those lessons back to fire safety on Earth.
details:
THE PROBLEM

Artemis lunar habitats are planned at about 34% oxygen and lower pressure, and Mars crews will live at partial gravity. Fire behaves very differently there: without gravity-driven airflow, a flame can survive where it would die on Earth, and some materials burn more easily in microgravity than Earth tests predict. NASA has run hundreds of careful combustion experiments on the ISS and in uncrewed spacecraft (BASS, BASS-II, Saffire), but the results are spread across reports, and nobody can easily ask: which materials are likely to burn on this mission, how sure are we, and what should NASA test next?

WHAT FLAMESENSE DOES

FlameSense is a free, public web app that turns NASA's microgravity combustion data into fire-safety insight that anyone can explore in a browser.

- Mission Mode: choose ISS, Artemis lunar habitat, Mars transit or Mars surface. For each cabin material, FlameSense shows the worst-case chance a flame keeps burning, the expected spread rate, how well NASA's data supports that answer, and a clear verdict.

- Experiment Wishlist: ranks the five untested conditions that would teach NASA the most, and exports a ready-to-use CSV test matrix.

- Mission Fire Brief: a one-click PDF of a mission's materials, data gaps, wishlist and citations, ready to hand to a team.

- Fire Lab: set material, oxygen, pressure, airflow and gravity, and see the chance a flame keeps burning, the spread rate with an 80% range, a physics check, the data support, and what moves the risk most. Compare it side by side with Earth.

- Gravity Twin: an Earth flame next to a flame at your chosen gravity, from Earth to Mars, Moon and orbit, so the physics is easy to see.

- Flammability Map: an oxygen x airflow heat map with every NASA run, the 50% burn line, and hatching wherever data is thin.

- Data Explorer: every NASA run with filters, charts, CSV export and a link to its source, plus all 24 combustion investigations in NASA's PSI Data Repository (1,991 rows) showing what NASA has and has not tested.

- Ask the NASA Papers: questions answered only from 68 NASA documents (60 NTRS reports), with every sentence cited.

- Lessons for Earth: what Apollo 1, Apollo 13, the 1997 Mir fire and NASA spinoffs teach us about fire safety in homes, vehicles and factories.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Data: one table of 123 NASA test runs from 10 experiment series on 14 fuels (97 microgravity, 26 partial gravity). Every row keeps its source file and citation; duplicates are logged and removed.

2. Models: LightGBM models predict the chance a flame keeps burning and the 10th, 50th and 90th percentile spread rate. They are trained with cross-validation grouped by test series, so the model is always scored on experiments it has never seen.

3. In the browser: the trained models are exported as JSON and run directly in the app (matching LightGBM to 1e-9), so predictions are instant, free and work without a server.

4. Honesty built in: a nearest-neighbour data-support index flags any prediction far from a real NASA run. Outside the range where NASA saw both outcomes, the app shows "Outside NASA's tested range" instead of a made-up number. A thin-fuel flame-spread theory (de Ris, 1969) acts as an independent physics check.

RESULTS

- Will the flame keep burning? ROC-AUC 0.82 and Brier score 0.19 (baseline 0.35) on unseen test series.

- Spread rate: mean error 0.16 mm/s (baseline 0.26), R2 0.78 on a log scale.

We also publish our limits openly: the dataset is small, Moon and Mars gravity are extrapolations, and the spread-rate range is still too narrow. A full model card and methods page are in the app and the repository.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

- Mission planners and engineers get a fast first look at material fire risk for a new cabin atmosphere, with the evidence behind it.

- NASA researchers get a ranked list of the most valuable next experiments, built from where the data is thinnest.

- Students and the public can see, interactively, why fire in space is different, using real NASA data instead of animations.

- On Earth, the same physics applies to low-airflow spaces such as sealed rooms, vehicles, aircraft cabins and factories.

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE

Most AI tools give an answer no matter what. FlameSense is built to know when it doesn't know: every prediction comes with its data support, a physics check and a citation, and the gaps themselves become a useful product, the Experiment Wishlist. It joins real lab data, machine learning, classic combustion theory and a cited document assistant in one app that runs in any browser.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES

Flutter Web (Dart) for the app; Python, pandas, scikit-learn and LightGBM for the data pipeline and models; Cloudflare Pages and Functions for hosting and the Ask API; Google Gemini API with Groq as fallback, used only over retrieved NASA documents; Playwright smoke tests; light and dark themes, keyboard and screen-reader support, and English and Bangla fonts.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Scientific honesty (no prediction without data support), traceability (every number links to a NASA source), accessibility, cost (free to run, no login), and safety: FlameSense is a research and education tool, not a certified fire-safety system, and is not affiliated with or endorsed by NASA.
